title: SQL and database injection prevention
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: All Unbound database access goes through one restricted, typed interface that only accepts bound parameters and fixed, reviewed query definitions; no application code can build SQL from strings. A semantic check on every commit finds raw command text, dynamic EXECUTE in database functions and any bypass of the approved interface, and blocks release on findings or on failure to run. Negative injection tests cover every input. Elimination of SQL injection is claimed only for the scanned scope, with the scan result and its exclusions published to customers under NDA.
current_practice: No Unbound code exists. The Secure Construction Standard v0.1 (proposed) states SEC-DB-001. Strata exists as a pilot declarative PostgreSQL schema tool (strata@c6a384ec) but no runtime typed query interface was found, so the enforcing mechanism named by SEC-DB-001 does not yet exist.
intended_practice: All Unbound database access goes through one restricted, typed interface that only accepts bound parameters and fixed, reviewed query definitions; no application code can build SQL from strings. A semantic check on every commit finds raw command text, dynamic EXECUTE in database functions and any bypass of the approved interface, and blocks release on findings or on failure to run. Negative injection tests cover every input. Elimination of SQL injection is claimed only for the scanned scope, with the scan result and its exclusions published to customers under NDA.
provable: Nothing for a production service; no Echelon production system exists as of 2026-11-25.
customer_statement: Echelon intends to implement this as part of Unbound's initial build; it is not in operation today and no evidence is available yet.
residual_risks: Enforcing component does not exist; SEC-DB-001 currently names a capability Strata does not provide.
Dynamic SQL in PostgreSQL functions, migrations and operational scripts.
open_questions: Which component will provide the runtime typed query interface: a Strata extension, an Unbound-owned ledger component (CNV-ARC-004) or a third-party library?

challenge.customer_intent: Know that injection cannot be used to read or tamper with financial and donor records.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Cross-tenant data disclosure or ledger tampering through injected SQL.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Secure coding guidance plus SAST and penetration testing finds many but not all injection paths; regressions recur.
challenge.legally_required: No statute requires a specific technique; GLBA and state safeguards rules require reasonable safeguards for customer information held by financial institutions and their service providers.
challenge.contractually_required: Commonly asked in bank and enterprise questionnaires; usually satisfied by attestation plus pen test results.
challenge.historical_convention: Parameterized queries, ORM usage, SAST and annual pen test.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Possible within a defined scope if string-built SQL is unavailable to application code and every path to the database is enumerated; trusted infrastructure, stored procedures and migrations must be in scope or listed as exclusions.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Semantic analysis over compiled F# and SQL source, fail-closed release gate.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-commit scan result with analyzer version and scope, signed and retained.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Restricted interface plus per-commit bypass scan plus negative tests, with elimination scoped to the scanned code.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, if the scanner is validated against seeded bypass fixtures and an independent tester attempts injection without restriction.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Engineering reviewers likely accept; procurement and auditors will still ask for an independent pen test result.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any raw ADO.NET or Npgsql use, dynamic EXECUTE in a database function, an unscanned project, or a reporting tool with direct database credentials.
challenge.conventional_cost: SAST license or tuning plus pen test fees.
challenge.alternative_cost: Building the restricted interface and analyzer; ongoing rule maintenance.
challenge.alternative_risks: Overconfidence: an elimination claim that silently excludes infrastructure code.
supporting_arguments: Making the unsafe operation unavailable is stronger than finding it after the fact.
Evidence is produced on every change rather than annually.
opposing_arguments: The enforcing component does not exist yet.
Assessors will not accept first-party elimination claims without independent reproduction.
Database-side code is easy to forget.

title: Command, code and interpreter injection prevention
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Unbound application code has no access to shell execution, dynamic code evaluation, runtime assembly loading or template evaluation of untrusted input; these capabilities are absent from the application dependency graph and detected by a semantic check if introduced. Log, header and directory-query outputs are built through encoding APIs. Any infrastructure exception uses fixed argument vectors, is reviewed and time-limited, and is listed in the release evidence.

title: Cross-site scripting prevention and output encoding
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Unbound never accepts user-supplied HTML (SEC-UI-001); free text is stored as text and rendered through encoding components. Application-authored browser script exists only inside Limen's kernel (SEC-UI-002), and application logic runs in F# compiled to WebAssembly that cannot touch the DOM directly. Source, generated bundles and interop glue are checked on every build for unsafe sinks and unapproved scripts, a nonce- or hash-based CSP blocks inline and injected script, and DAST tests URL, attribute and DOM contexts. Echelon states the scope and residual risks rather than claiming XSS is eliminated.
current_practice: No Unbound UI exists. Limen exists (limen@743cdb9b) and separates browser kernel from application engine; its kernel and protocol are TypeScript and its F# WebAssembly consumers are demonstration sites. No CSP, DAST or sink checking for an Echelon product was located.
intended_practice: Unbound never accepts user-supplied HTML (SEC-UI-001); free text is stored as text and rendered through encoding components. Application-authored browser script exists only inside Limen's kernel (SEC-UI-002), and application logic runs in F# compiled to WebAssembly that cannot touch the DOM directly. Source, generated bundles and interop glue are checked on every build for unsafe sinks and unapproved scripts, a nonce- or hash-based CSP blocks inline and injected script, and DAST tests URL, attribute and DOM contexts. Echelon states the scope and residual risks rather than claiming XSS is eliminated.

customer_statement: Echelon intends to implement this as part of Unbound's initial build; it is not in operation today and no evidence is available yet.
residual_risks: Limen kernel script, Folio HTML output and email templates are rendering paths that need their own checks.
Third-party scripts such as analytics or support widgets would breach the model if added.

challenge.customer_intent: Prevent account takeover and fraudulent grant recommendations through script injection.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Session theft or forged actions in a donor or sponsor session.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Framework auto-encoding plus scanning is reasonably effective but DOM-based XSS and unsafe helper use are frequently missed.
challenge.contractually_required: Commonly asked; usually answered with pen test results.
challenge.historical_convention: Output encoding guidance, SAST, DAST, annual pen test.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Partial. Refusing HTML input and confining script to a small kernel removes most sinks, but the Standard itself says this alone does not eliminate XSS; URL, attribute and DOM contexts and the kernel's own code remain.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Build-time sink and script inventory checks over generated bundles, CSP as a runtime backstop.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-build check result with bundle digest and deployed CSP capture.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Small, audited kernel plus CSP plus per-build bundle inspection.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes for the inspected bundle; requires independent testing for the kernel and context handling.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely as defense in depth; unlikely as a replacement for independent testing.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any added third-party script, an unsafe sink in Limen, a CSP relaxation, or a Folio template rendering untrusted strings unencoded.
challenge.conventional_cost: Scanner licenses and pen test fees.
challenge.alternative_risks: Limen becomes a single high-value component; a defect there affects every application.
supporting_arguments: WebAssembly application code cannot call DOM APIs directly.
opposing_arguments: Kernel is TypeScript; script still exists.
WebAssembly runtimes may need CSP relaxations.
No independent test of Limen exists.

title: Cross-site request forgery and cross-origin protections
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Every state-changing browser request carries an anti-forgery token or verified origin, session cookies are SameSite and host-prefixed, CORS admits only listed Echelon origins without credentials for others, framing is denied, and high-risk actions (new payee, grant above threshold, authority change) require explicit step-up confirmation. Configuration is captured daily and tested on every release.

title: Business logic and workflow integrity
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Workflow states are explicit types with only legal transitions representable; every authorization, eligibility, fee and amount is recomputed on the server inside the command transaction (CNV-PLT-010); updates bind only to declared fields; and financial invariants are tested with property-based, concurrency and replay tests on every change. Business-logic weaknesses are treated as a verification problem, not a scanning problem.

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure no one can move money or approve grants outside the sponsor's policy.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Unauthorized or duplicated disbursement, skipped approval, manipulated fee.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Scanners rarely find business-logic flaws; pen tests find some within limited time.
challenge.legally_required: Sponsors bear IRC 4966/4967 exposure for improper distributions; the platform's control is how they meet it, not a statute on Echelon.
challenge.contractually_required: Expected by sponsors and their auditors.
challenge.historical_convention: Manual test cases, UAT and pen testing.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Illegal transitions can be made unrepresentable in types; wrong but legal policy cannot.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Type system, transaction-bound server recomputation, property tests in CI.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Invariant test results per commit with generator seeds.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Explicit state machines plus generated adversarial sequences.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, tests are reproducible from seeds.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely if presented with reproducible results; auditors will still sample transactions.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Any path that writes authoritative state outside the command handler, or client-computed values accepted by an API.
challenge.conventional_cost: Manual QA and pen test time.
challenge.alternative_risks: Generators that miss realistic sequences give false confidence.
supporting_arguments: Covers a class scanners cannot see.
Directly tied to sponsor financial risk.
opposing_arguments: Property tests only check the properties someone thought to write.

title: Session management
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Sessions are server-controlled, rotated at sign-in and privilege change, bound to secure host-prefixed HttpOnly SameSite cookies, expire on idle and absolute timeouts appropriate to the role, and are revoked immediately on logout, deprovisioning or administrative action. No bearer token is placed in script-readable browser storage. Tests prove fixation resistance and revocation latency.

title: Error handling and information exposure
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Failures are explicit result values with stable machine-readable codes; responses never contain stack traces, SQL, internal hostnames or other tenants' identifiers; logs are redacted before write; unknown or failed states deny the action. Aegis provides fault capture and redaction primitives for .NET; tests assert response content and periodic log scans look for secrets and restricted data.

title: Application security verification standard and testing evidence
status_rationale: Echelon has no production deployment; the relevant rules exist only in the proposed Secure Construction Standard v0.1 or Unbound requirements, so this is a target state.
target_answer: Each production release is verified against OWASP ASVS Level 2 (Level 3 for payment, authority and ledger functions), with a per-requirement matrix showing whether the property is structurally enforced, automatically tested, manually reviewed or independently tested. challenge.customer_intent: Obtain independent confidence that the application resists common attacks.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Annual pen tests are time-boxed snapshots; quality varies with tester skill.
challenge.legally_required: Not by statute for Echelon; NYDFS 500.8 and FTC Safeguards 314.4(c)(4) require covered customers to evaluate externally developed applications, which drives the request.
challenge.contractually_required: Bank and insurer contracts commonly require an annual independent pen test summary.
challenge.historical_convention: Annual third-party pen test with executive summary letter.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Not applicable; verification is still needed.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Per-release ASVS matrix generated from structural checks and automated tests.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-release matrix with method and independence labels.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Continuous first-party verification plus a focused independent test supplied with threat models and the matrix.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: First-party evidence is reproducible but not independent.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Independent test still expected; continuous matrix is an addition, not a substitute.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If structural claims are not independently reproduced, they should not reduce pen test scope.
challenge.alternative_risks: Customers may misread first-party evidence as independent assurance.
supporting_arguments: Evidence per release rather than per year.
opposing_arguments: Institutions require independence; internal evidence cannot replace it (Standard, External assurance section).
